question: A 68-year-old woman comes to the physician because of lower back pain that began suddenly 2 weeks ago after getting up from her chair. She has hypertension, chronic bilateral knee pain, and a history of breast cancer 15 years ago that was treated with lumpectomy. Her mother has rheumatoid arthritis. Medications include hydrochlorothiazide and acetaminophen. She appears well. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows tenderness to palpation of the lower spine. Both knees are enlarged and swollen. Neurologic examination shows sensorineural hearing impairment of the left ear. Her gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) is 30 U/L (N: 0–30 U/L), alkaline phosphatase (ALP) is 310 U/L, and serum calcium is 10.2 mg/dL. A spinal x-ray shows a fracture in the L4 vertebra. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Lumbar spine fracture -> Lower back pain -> L4 vertebra involvement -> 80% CHAIN: Chronic bilateral knee pain -> Enlarged and swollen knees -> Possible inflammatory joint disease -> 70% CHAIN: Sensorineural hearing impairment of the left ear -> Possible genetic predisposition -> 60% CHAIN: Elevated GGT and ALP -> Possible liver involvement -> 50% CHAIN: History of breast cancer -> Possible bone metastases -> 40% CHAIN: Normal vital signs -> Excludes acute life-threatening conditions -> 90% CHAIN: Combination of findings -> Paget disease of bone -> 80%
enhanced_information: The most likely diagnosis for the 68-year-old woman with lower back pain, lumbar spine fracture, chronic bilateral knee pain, sensorineural hearing impairment, elevated GGT and ALP levels, and history of breast cancer is Paget disease of bone. The combination of findings supports this diagnosis with 80% certainty.
analysis: The core medical principle guiding this case is the recognition of Paget disease of bone as the most likely diagnosis based on the patient's clinical presentation, including lower back pain, lumbar spine fracture, chronic bilateral knee pain, sensorineural hearing impairment, elevated GGT and ALP levels, and history of breast cancer. Paget disease of bone is characterized by disorganized bone remodeling, leading to bone pain, deformities, and fractures. The enhanced information provided further supports this diagnosis with a high level of certainty.
